scores.scale: 0 unusable; 5 mixed but playable with substantial friction; 7 good with meaningful rough edges; 10 exceptional and consistently clear within assessed scope. Subjective observed-interface grades, not win/loss grades or certification.

reasons.overall_mobile: A coherent, atmospheric mission was navigable and completable with useful mobile assists. Combat inputs worked in short manually directed samples, but substantial aim/route assistance and frequent paused observation limit conclusions about sustained mobile play.
reasons.controls: MOVE plus FIRE drag worked for visible patrols; swipes turned predictably in the sampled scene; DASH gave visible cooldown feedback. Aim taps rotate the view substantially, and dash/route interaction was uncertain. Continuous hold comfort and thumb ergonomics unassessed.
reasons.gameplay: Recoveries, distinct coil phases and defending an upload provided understandable stages. Choosing visible patrols and seeing explicit down feedback was satisfying in the observed short interactions. Protected-phase firing, reload interruptions and offscreen attackers added friction. No inference about longer-term enjoyment.
reasons.presentation: Rain, lighting, teal/orange palette and station signage provide a coherent atmosphere. Low-poly silhouettes are readable at close range; audio and hardware smoothness unassessed.
reasons.usability: Route/approach transitions, clear objective names, recovery checkmarks, map route and terminal stats support progress. No checkpoint or recovery menu needed, so those flows unassessed.
reasons.readability: Large health/ammo, objective and target feedback are legible at 844x390. Small world labels and dense overlapping right-side controls/threat cues take more attention.

coverage.manual_move_fire_drag: Entry guard TARGET DOWN; visible perimeter patrol selected after left scene turn, simultaneous MOVE and FIRE drag registered SENTINEL DOWN. Ammo 21 to 18 on patrol; assisted aim used. No individual shot misses distinguishable; end UI reports 100% accuracy.
coverage.scene_turn: 354 to 015 with right swipe; 315 to 278 with left swipe to expose patrol. Patrol tap and fire drag changed heading to 245; required reorientation.
coverage.dash: Tapped visible DASH after scene turn; cyan effect, displacement toward wall, cooldown 4.3 visible. No phase evade credited; no claim of successful dodge.
coverage.map: Opened planning map, inspected selected Extraction and 23m route, closed visibly.
coverage.mission: Used HOLD ROUTE/HOLD APPROACH for recoveries, aimed and fired at coils, auto reload at zero, remained on deck to upload.

helpful: Directional threat cues and route/approach prompts
Map extraction selection and route length
Explicit armor/charge/open boss HUD and upload percent
friction: Needed a left scene turn to locate patrol beyond offscreen cue
Small dark world labels harder to read than HUD
Fire into armor/charge reduced coil II only to 15% before reload; next burst completed it
Rear threats caused shield damage while focusing coils; upload also took damage
uncertainties: Not all spent rounds can be classified as hits versus protected-phase fire from screenshots
Automatic capture breaks holds; no continuous rearming assessment
Dash was sampled outside a charge interception; no evasion success established

attempts.fresh_start: Visible START FRESH tapped as #play-again in act with capture, after attempt one was saved to this report. No checkpoint retry.

Visible west patrol at left edge: target tap plus simultaneous MOVE/FIRE drag, 21 to 19 ammo, SENTINEL DOWN. Visible east patrol: target tap plus simultaneous MOVE/FIRE drag, 19 to 16 ammo, SENTINEL DOWN. Deck: stationary FIRE drag after tap registered INTERCEPTOR DOWN; another fresh-view target tap/FIRE registered another INTERCEPTOR DOWN.
coverage.scene_turn: No independent scene swipe this attempt; tap aims changed headings (303 to 256 on west patrol, 108 to 148 on east patrol, 346 to 004 then 353 on deck). Independent scene-swipe coverage was attempt one.
coverage.dash: Visible DASH tapped in open travel after entry guard. Next screenshot showed cooldown 1.5 and West Archive 45m away. Route did not make expected progress in same batch; separate hold resumed travel. Cause uncertain; no successful evade inferred. End stats credit zero phase evades.
coverage.mission: Followed visible route and approach prompts, recovered all three, shot current visible coils, automatic reload, returned to deck and fired at two visible threats while uploading.
coverage.unassessed: No map, tools, zoom, jump, settings changes or independent scene swipe in this attempt.

helpful: Target-down messages confirmed west/east patrol and deck engagements
Receiver badges and objective names made progress explicit
Coil II remaining 37% identified unfinished work before automatic reload
Upload percent and stay-on-deck instruction were clear
friction: Aim assist substantially changed heading, requiring reorientation
Dash-plus-route batch ended with archive still 45m away; route resumed in next batch, cause uncertain
Shield fell to 34 on boss approach despite eliminating both visible perimeter patrols
Coil II burst exhausted magazine at 37%; another burst needed after reload
Threat cue and many controls occupy substantial scene area
misses_and_corrections: No individual missed shot distinguishable; terminal UI reported 100% accuracy, with 16 assisted shots, so this is not an unaided precision claim
Did not disable coil II in first burst; resumed firing after reload and saw COIL II OFF
Resumed route hold separately after dash/travel batch
Rechecked view after each target tap changed projection before selecting next target
uncertainties: Dash effect versus route interaction not isolated
Some screenshots and beforePause metadata differed slightly (e.g. upload percent/shield), consistent with capture occurring live; screenshots remain evidence rather than exact simultaneous state
Continuous held-burst rearming comfort cannot be established because every capture releases contacts

Dash plus route travel made unclear progress in one batch; cause not isolated.
Successful charge evasion, continuous holds and physical-device quality remain unassessed.
